A0224.title: Benign Crawler Whitelisting
A0224.definition: Identifying legitimate search-engine and compliant crawlers via IP allowlists, User-Agent recognition, and reverse DNS (rDNS) verification, then allowing them through — preventing anti-scraping policies from falsely blocking benign bots and causing SEO or indexing losses.
A0224.description: While anti-scraping policies block malicious crawlers, they risk false positives against legitimate search-engine crawlers (e.g., Googlebot, Bingbot, Baiduspider, Sogou Spider), leading to de-indexed pages and reduced search traffic. Benign crawler whitelisting identifies legitimate crawlers via three checks: an IP allowlist verifying the request source IP belongs to the search engine's officially published crawler IP ranges; User-Agent recognition matching official crawler UA patterns; and reverse DNS (rDNS) resolution of the request IP with forward-confirmation round-trip to prevent attackers spoofing a Googlebot UA to bypass detection. Combined, these three checks effectively distinguish real search-engine crawlers from malicious crawlers disguised as search engines. This measure complements proxy detection (A0038) and IP intelligence (A0016-001), and is a prerequisite for cloud anti-scraping (A0003) policy — first allow benign crawlers, then identify and restrict the remaining traffic, lowering the false-block rate.
A0224.limitation: Benign crawler whitelisting depends on timely maintenance of search-engine official IP ranges and rDNS data; failure to sync IP-range changes causes false blocks or false allows. Some compliant crawlers do not publish IP ranges or use third-party CDN egress, making them hard to include in the allowlist. Attackers who can control rDNS records or use proxies within search-engine IP ranges can still spoof and bypass, so it cannot be trusted alone and must combine UA and IP verification.
